summary: Cardiastracont is an offline-first, autonomous space health ecosystem and AI Flight Surgeon for deep space missions (e.g. Mars transit with 4-22 minute communication latency). It's a continuous monitor of multimodal biometrics via an Apple Watch app, Meta Quest 3 VR as HUD and camera. It provides emergency triage, hands free voice guidance with Quindar tones, radiation drug degradation tracking and 60 second guided box breathing. It's all about ensuring astronaut survivability in deep space and bringing life saving medical autonomy to isolated submarines, polar outposts and disaster zones.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

Cardiastracont is an offline-first autonomous space medicine command ecosystem and AI Flight Surgeon designed for deep-space missions (such as Mars transit) where Earth evacuation is impossible and communication latency reaches up to 22 minutes each way.

  • Multi-Modal Biometric Ingestion: Continuously captures Heart Rate (BPM), Blood Oxygen (SpO2), HRV Stress, Respiration, and dynamic ECG waveforms across an Apple Watch app (watchOS HealthKit), an astronaut mobile health pad, and a contactless optical camera pipeline (rPPG) measuring pulse through facial skin color variations.
    1. Deterministic NASA Rules Engine (<1ms response): Instant clinical decision protocols based on NASA Exploration Medical Capability (ExMC) Tier 4/5 guidelines for acute crises (Hypoxia, Ventricular Tachycardia, Hypercapnia, and Panic Storms).
    2. Offline Local Vector RAG & NVIDIA NIM AI: A local vector database of NASA spaceflight medical manuals paired with NVIDIA NIM microservices (nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b / Llama-3.1) for deep differential diagnosis and treatment checklists.
  • Real-Time Cross-Platform Sync: Broadcasts telemetry and alerts at 30Hz via WebSockets to synchronize Meta Quest 3 holographic VR HUDs (OpenXR) and responsive mission control consoles.

What benefits does it have?

  • Zero-Latency Clinical Triage: Eliminates the deadly 40-minute roundtrip communication blackout during life-threatening medical emergencies.
  • Hands-Free Aerospace Voice Surgeon: Features two-way voice dialog (STT/TTS) calibrated with authentic Apollo-style Quindar radio cues, allowing hands-free clinical support during critical flight operations.
  • Psychological Stabilization (Sanctuary Mode): Deploys an interactive 60-second guided 4-7-8 box breathing countermeasure with relaxing Web Audio harmonic soundscapes to halt acute panic attacks.
  • Automated NASA Form 1042 Export: Automatically compiles mission vitals, diagnostic histories, and treatments into official NASA Flight Physical & Aeromedical Incident reports with 1-click download.
  • Pharmaceutical Efficacy Modeling: Tracks Galactic Cosmic Ray (GCR) radiation exposure in millisieverts (mSv) and models the potency loss of Emergency Medical Kit (EMK) drugs, calculating compensatory dosages.

What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Deep-Space Exploration: Shifts human spaceflight medicine from Earth-dependence to complete clinical self-sufficiency, ensuring crew survival on journeys to Mars and beyond.
  • Terrestrial Impact (Earth Spinoffs): The zero-internet, low-resource architecture directly transfers to extreme isolated environments on Earth—including deep-sea submarines, polar research outposts, offshore oil rigs, and disaster relief zones lacking physicians and connectivity.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Programming Languages: Python 3.10+, JavaScript (ES6+), Swift (SwiftUI), C# (Unity), and GLSL / ShaderLab.
  • Backend & Cloud Infrastructure: FastAPI, Uvicorn, WebSockets, Pydantic, Python-Dotenv, and Render.com.
  • AI & Clinical Knowledge: NVIDIA NIM API (Nemotron / Llama-3.1), Local Vector RAG Knowledge Base (TF-IDF & semantic embeddings), NASA ExMC Clinical Guidelines.
  • Frontend & Web APIs: HTML5 Canvas (dynamic ECG rendering), Web Audio API (Master Caution dual-tone klaxon synthesizer & Quindar tones), Web Speech API (STT/TTS), and Progressive Web App (PWA) standards.
  • Hardware Platforms: Apple Watch (HealthKit), Meta Quest 3 (OpenXR / Unity 2022.3), and standard laptop/smartphone webcams (optical rPPG).

How is your project creative?

  • Contactless Optical rPPG Pulse Monitoring: Transforms standard cabin webcams into touchless heart monitors if wearables run out of battery or an astronaut is incapacitated.
  • Space Radiation Drug Degradation Engine: Rather than assuming static medical supplies, it accounts for the physical reality of cosmic rays degrading pharmaceuticals over multi-year missions.
  • Acoustically Ergonomic Klaxon & Quindar Audio: Implements genuine aerospace Human Factors standards, including alternating 2500Hz/1500Hz master caution tones with acoustic acknowledge/mute controls.
  • Earth-Mars Latency Simulator: Features an adjustable 0s to 22-minute signal queue, proving why onboard AI autonomy is an existential requirement.

What factors did your team consider?

  • 100% Offline-First Resilience: Zero reliance on cloud servers or external networks; all diagnostic logic runs locally inside the spacecraft.
  • Cognitive Load & Human Factors: High-contrast cyber-aerospace HUDs that prioritize instant glanceability and minimize sensory overwhelm during alarms.
  • Hardware Redundancy & Failover: Seamless handoff—if the VR headset or Apple Watch loses power, the mobile health pad or webcam rPPG takes over immediately.
  • Medical Ethics & AI Safety Boundaries: Strict deterministic clinical guardrails ensure AI recommendations strictly conform to verified space medicine protocols without hallucinations.
